newsitem.title: USA: U.S. attache-Argentina 96/97 soybean crop 12.5 MMT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. attache-Argentina 96/97 soybean crop 12.5 MMT.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache lowered his estimate for Argentina 1996/97 soybean production to 12.5 million tonnes from 13.25 million tonnes seen earlier, citing serious damage to the crop due to drought.

"Soybean production has received serious damage due to the drought in the provinces of Santa Fe and Cordoba, and parts of northern Buenos Aires province as well," the attache wrote in a report dated April 29 that was released in Washington Wednesday.
"Some areas in the main soybean belt have gone without meaningful rain for two months or more, and this has severely impacted actual yield results which are now becoming available," he continued.

In mid-April, the Argentine goverment lowered its forecast for soybean production to 12.87 million tonnes. The attache noted in the report that some private trade estimates are averaging almost one million tonnes lower.

Attache reports are not official USDA data. In its monthly World Supply and Demand report released April 11, USDA pegged the Argentina 1996/97 soybean crop at 13.25 million tonnes. USDA will release the May Supply and Demand report on Monday.
In the report, the attache also shaved his forecast for Argentina soybean exports to 1.0 million tonnes based on lower than expected production and increased crushing.

The attache also lowered his forecast for Argentina 1996/97 sunflower production to 5.1 million tonnes from 5.4 million tonnes "due to lighter grain and poor filling brought about by wet weather during the pollination stage."
